To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pretreatments of pineapple slices by sulphiting at different levels and sucrose/osmotic pretreatments significantly influenced the Deff values of air drying of the slices at 50 and 70 o C.
the effective moisture diffusion coefficient (De ff) of air drying of pine apple slices was significantly affected by sulphiting pretreatment, osmotic pretreatment, and drying temperature.

The effective diffusion coefficient (D eff ) of air drying of smooth cayenne pineapple slices was strongly affected by the sulphiting pretreatments at 2500ppm and osmotic pretreatment with 40% sucroses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for the determination of effective diffusion coefficient (D eff) during the drying of food materials.
the effects of sulphur dioxide and sucrose pretreatment on the effective diffusion coefficient of air drying of smooth cayenne pineapple slices.
the study of the effect of sulphiting and/or osmotic pre-treatment on pineapple slices during air drying.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sulphiting and osmotics pretreatments had a significant impact on the effective moisture diffusivity of air dried pineapple slices.
the pretreatments improved the effective diffusion coefficient of pineapple slices during air drying, with sulphiting at 2,500 ppm having the highest effect.
the sulphiting pretreatments at 2500ppm and 40% sucroses/osmosis pretreatment improved the Deff values of pineapple slices, with sulphiting pretreatment being the best.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sulphiting of pineapple slices at 2500ppm improved the Deff value of the slices, which is in agreement with the work of (Adeyemi and Oluwaniyi, 2010).
the sulphiting and osmose pre-treatments improved the drying kinetics of pineapple slices, with sulphiting pretreatment having the highest value at 2500ppm.

the effective diffusion coefficient (D EFF ) was strongly affected by pretreatments and the sulphiting at 2 500 ppm equaled 9.10 + 0.13 × 10 − 6 and 6.78 + 0.53 × 10 −6 cm/s for drying at 70 °C and 50 °C, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pretreatment methods improve the effective moisture diffusion coefficient (DeFF) of air-drying pineapple slices, with sulphiting at 2,500 ppm having the highest DeFF value.
the effective moisture diffusivity is a very good tool for predicting the drying kinetics and the drying time of the pineapple slices.
pretreatment methods can improve the Deff value of pineapple slices.
